result.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
result.summary: Particle filters flexibly represent complex, multimodal beliefs but expose them as weighted, unordered sets incompatible with conventional fixed-dimensional policies. We study particle-belief encodings as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies while holding belief estimation and policy optimization fixed. We compare statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function (CGF) features, and permutation-invariant set encoders. Trainable encoders are learned end-to-end or pretrained through belief reconstruction or task-specific prediction. Across eight tasks, pooling-based set encoders and gradient CGF features are reliable end-to-end, while the Set Transformer achieves the highest performance with appropriate pretraining. Task-specific pretraining helps when its target captures decision-relevant belief structure, whereas reconstruction pretraining and latent alignment provide more selective benefits. For selecting and training particle-belief encoders in partially observable Markov decision processes, our results show that an encoding that reconstructs the belief well is not necessarily a good input for control.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在部分可观测强化学习中固定信念估计与策略优化，比较统计摘要、CGF 特征和置换不变集合编码器对粒子信念的表示方式，并在八个任务上考察端到端训练与重构、任务特定预测等预训练方式对策略性能的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「重构得好不等于好的控制输入」及预训练目标筛选的结论，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态应保留何种任务必要信息、以及视觉证据编码器的训练目标选择；但该工作无视觉输入与 latent 推理生成，联动仅为概念层面。
